ai.description: This turtle reaches 20 cm. It has a dark brown, keeled carapace and a yellow plastron. Distinctive features include yellow concentric rings on each scute and a bright yellow head pattern.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Morenia petersi* is the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange "eye-spot" on each side of the head, contrasting with its dark skin.
ai.habitat: *Morenia petersi* inhabits slow-moving rivers, ponds, and marshes in the Gangetic and Brahmaputra plains, favoring areas with dense aquatic vegetation and soft mud bottoms.
ai.behavior: The Indian eyed turtle is primarily diurnal, often basking on logs or rocks during the day to regulate its body temperature before foraging for aquatic vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Morenia petersi* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the winter months, generally between December and February in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Morenia petersi* is found in the Gangetic and Brahmaputra river systems of northern and northeastern India, primarily across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
